newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran's Qeshm free zone attracts $100 mln investment.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Qeshm free zone attracts $100 mln investment.

text.p: Foreign investments total only $100 million in Iran's Qeshm island free zone which has capacity to attract investments worth $4 billion, the zone's managing director was on Wednesday quoted as saying.

"So far foreign investors have undertaken to invest $1.5 billion in Qeshm, but negotiations have indicated that Qeshm affords areas for foreign investment amounting to $4 billion," Behrooz Bushehri said.
"Practically, however, only $100 million has been invested by the end of the last Iranian year (ending March 1997)," the English-language Iran News quoted him as saying.
Bushehri said the free zone was in negotiations with a number of foreign banks and investors eager to invest in the zone, one of three Iran set up in 1989 to attract foreign investment.
He said the zone's airport, inaugurated earlier this month, would start operations next week.

"Last year the 30 factories which had become operational in Qeshm produced goods that were exported fetching $3.5 million. When the number of active companies reaches 50 this year, export earnings will also soar," he said.
"Our main objective is to promote non-oil exports in the free zones," he added.

He said among the foreign investments in Qeshm was a joint venture with two Indian companies to build a $350 million fertiliser plant, a $60 million Lebanese plant producing ship plates and steel and a $10 million Chinese venture producing steel and zinc.

Iran has said it planned to allow foreign banks to establish branches in the free zones and authorise partly private-owned Iranian banks in the zones. The plan appeared to be the result of legislation passed by parliament last year to ease foreign exchange rules in the zones to attract foreign investment.
